notes.scope: Task 4 — TelegramUpdate, Message, Chat, User records + TelegramUpdateDeserializationTest (commit b8a2f4e).

checks.name: Mass-assignment defense (Decision 6)
checks.evidence: @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) present on all four records (TelegramUpdate L16, Message L8, Chat L10, User L11). Tests deserialize_unknownTopLevelField_isIgnored (extra top-level 'some_future_field' + 'another_unknown') and deserialize_unknownNestedField_isIgnored (extra 'junk' in message and 'future_field' in chat) both deserialise without throwing, confirming both top-level and nested unknowns are swallowed.

checks.name: No Object/Map catch-all
checks.evidence: Non-message slots typed JsonNode (a sealed Jackson tree node), not Object/Map. Worker must call explicit .get(...) accessors; no implicit POJO binding surface. Records contain no Object/Map components.

checks.name: No @JsonCreator / @JsonAutoDetect / @JsonTypeInfo
checks.evidence: grep -rn for @JsonCreator|@JsonAutoDetect|@JsonTypeInfo|enableDefaultTyping|activateDefaultTyping under backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/webhook/ returned no matches. Jackson defaults preserved.

checks.name: OWASP A08 — Insecure deserialisation / polymorphism
checks.evidence: Java records are implicitly final; no @JsonTypeInfo / default typing; no untrusted-class instantiation vector. ObjectMapper used in tests is `new ObjectMapper()` with default config (default typing off). JsonNode is inert tree data, not a POJO factory.

checks.name: OWASP A03 — Injection surface
checks.evidence: DTOs are pure data carriers; no SQL/command/template execution. Snake-case field name matching uses Jackson's record-component name binding (no @JsonProperty aliases, no reflection escape hatch).

checks.name: Test fixtures — secrets / PII
checks.evidence: Fixtures use synthetic data only: 'Alice'/'Liddell'/'alice', language 'uk', numeric IDs (100200300, 9876543210, 123456789, -100), callback id 'cb-1', text '/start ref_abc', 'hi'. No real bot tokens, API keys, production user IDs, phone numbers or e-mail addresses present.

checks.name: Hardcoded secrets scan
checks.evidence: No API_KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN, private-key blocks, or connection strings in any of the five new files.

informational_observations: Chat.type is String rather than an enum — deliberate forward-compat choice documented in Javadoc; not a security concern.
Boolean is_bot is boxed so a missing field stays null and is not silently coerced to false — correct for trust-boundary integrity.
JsonNode slots will need concrete records in Epic 05/06; mass-assignment defense must be carried over to those records when they are introduced.
Records are pure data; no toString/logging override that could leak content downstream — no logging concerns introduced by this task.
